about: Hand-curated benchmark scores for frontier language models. Each score says who reported it: lab = the model's own lab; other = a competitor lab's published table; independent = a third-party evaluator. sec 1 = the figure reached us through a secondary source (⚠️). Scores run under different harnesses, effort settings or subsets are not directly comparable: read the note.
benchmarks: Agent harness and effort setting change results a lot; see each score's note
Length of task (in human-expert hours) the agent completes with 50% success on METR's task suite; wide confidence intervals
Short fact questions; percent correct (abstaining counts as wrong), so willingness to guess moves scores
Google DeepMind / Kaggle; tracked by Epoch AI
Kaggle-style ML engineering tasks; share of tasks earning a medal. Frontier labs mostly report full MLE-bench or PaperBench only in system cards
Multi-step tool use against real MCP servers
Interactive puzzle games that are easy for people and new to the model; the ARC Prize team's main AGI test. Scores differ by harness and effort setting
Abstract grid puzzles; reported close to saturation by late 2026
2,500 expert-written questions across many fields; scores depend on tools, effort and subset
Center for AI Safety and Scale AI
Research-level mathematics; Epoch AI reports every Tier 4 problem has now been solved by some model (saturated)

Agents get a base model, a GPU budget and a target task and must post-train the model themselves; scored on the trained model. Run by the benchmark authors, not the labs (a few entries may be provider-submitted)
Long real-world tasks from professional occupations (consulting, finance, design), graded against expert work; run by OpenAI, so scores are lab-reported
Rating from blind side-by-side votes by users; top models sit within overlapping margins, so small gaps are noise
